_matching: Each entry lists evidence groups. A question must hit at least one term from EVERY group of an entry to be answered from it. The first group is the topic group; generic phrases such as 'how many' are never enough on their own.

entries.title: How profile data is used
entries.answer: Profile data in this fictional demo is used only to show your own profile back to you and to let admins search basic, non-sensitive fields. It is never sold or shared with third parties.

entries.title: Deleting profile sections
entries.answer: You can delete your demographic, wellness preference, and emergency contact sections from the Profile page. Each deletion is recorded in the audit trail without storing the deleted values.

entries.title: Emergency contacts limit
entries.answer: Each member can store up to 5 emergency contacts. Contacts are visible only to you, not to other members.

entries.title: What admins can see
entries.answer: Admins sign in with a separate session login and can list profiles with search, city filter, and pagination. Admin actions are written to the audit trail.

entries.title: Forgotten password
entries.answer: Password reset is not available in this demo yet. Create a new demo account with a different email if you lose access.

entries.title: What the engagement prediction means
entries.answer: The engagement prediction estimates, from fictional synthetic data, whether a demo member is likely to use the wellness app in the next 30 days. It is an educational example and says nothing about health.

entries.title: What the clusters mean
entries.answer: Clusters group synthetic members by app usage patterns (sessions, session length, days since signup). They are descriptive only and are not used to make decisions about anyone.

entries.title: Wellness reminders
entries.answer: Wellness reminders are optional. You choose the channel (email, sms, or app) in your wellness preferences and can turn them off at any time.
